<html:div xmlns:html="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml">
<html:p>Sometime around 2010, while I was working at Google, I came up with a fun mini project to
marry my love of retro computing with my excitement for working at big G.</html:p>

<html:p>I smuggled my BBC Master into the office and hooked it up over a serial cable to my
work desktop, and then after some jiggery-pokery, was able to get a terminal
emulator running. The BBC was a dumb terminal to the work machine, and I ran <html:code>lynx</html:code>
and visited <html:code>google.com</html:code>, searched for <html:code>google</html:code>. I think I can safely say I'm the
only person who googled Google on a BBC Micro from within Google itself.</html:p>

<html:p class="picture">
<html:a href="/202608/moog-label.jpeg">
<html:img src="/202608/moog-label-thumb.jpeg" width="600" height="452" alt="The power supply of my BBC Master, with a handwritten moog@ label still stuck to the case" />
</html:a>
<html:br />My Beeb still has the <html:code>moog@</html:code> sticker (my LDAP login) to show whose it was.
</html:p>


<html:p>I was trying to replicate this at home but sadly Google no longer supports non-JS
browsers like <html:code>lynx</html:code> (I guess I could find another one that does?). But I did see
that DuckDuckGo has a "lite" mode. After an enormous amount of fiddling I was able
to recreate something similar:</html:p>

<html:p class="picture">
<html:a href="/202608/beeb-duckduckgo.png">
<html:img src="/202608/beeb-duckduckgo-thumb.png" width="720" height="576" alt="A BBC Master screen showing DuckDuckGo Lite search results for 'bbc micro emulators' in lynx" />
</html:a>
<html:br />The glory of DuckDuckGo on a Beeb.
</html:p>


<html:p>The image above was captured with my own in-progress software PAL decoder <html:a href="https://github.com/mattgodbolt/PALindrome">PALindrome</html:a>,
so the blurriness etc is likely from my inept implementation.</html:p>

<html:p>I used a cheap no-name USB serial converter<html:sup id="fnref:cheap"><html:a class="footnote-ref" href="#fn:cheap">1</html:a></html:sup> and an RS232-RS423 DIN cable. I first put the cable in 180
degrees the wrong way (bad keying on the cable, oops), but once correctly plugged in things started working. I initially tried with the
Master's built-in <html:code>*TERMINAL</html:code> program, but it's frankly pretty rubbish for this. I used the Acornsoft
"Termulator" ROM instead. 4800 baud was the fastest I could reliably get working, and it needed a bit of
work to get XON/XOFF configured. With some LLM help I got a <html:code>getty</html:code> running so I could log in with the Beeb.
It's hard to type your muscle-memory password on a not-quite-normal keyboard! A hack to tell <html:code>lynx</html:code> not
to process XON/XOFF and not show colour:</html:p>

<html:div class="codehilite"><html:pre><html:span /><html:code><html:span class="na">INCLUDE</html:span><html:span class="o">:</html:span><html:span class="s">/etc/lynx/lynx.cfg</html:span>
<html:span class="na">KEYMAP</html:span><html:span class="o">:</html:span><html:span class="s">^S:DO_NOTHING</html:span>
<html:span class="na">KEYMAP</html:span><html:span class="o">:</html:span><html:span class="s">^Q:DO_NOTHING</html:span>
<html:span class="na">SHOW_COLOR</html:span><html:span class="o">:</html:span><html:span class="s">never</html:span>
</html:code></html:pre></html:div>


<html:p class="picture">
<html:a href="/202608/whole-setup.jpeg">
<html:img src="/202608/whole-setup-thumb.jpeg" width="600" height="452" alt="A desk with a lidless BBC Master, a multimeter, a sticker-covered laptop and a tangle of wires" />
</html:a>
<html:br />The whole Heath Robinson setup.
</html:p>


<html:p>A bit of double-nostalgia for me: 2010 is when my youngest was born, and we just celebrated his 16th...
where does the time go?</html:p>

<html:p>Despite all my <html:a href="https://compiler-explorer.com">Compiler Explorer</html:a> commitments, and my
<html:a href="https://hudsonrivertrading.com">fun new(ish) job</html:a>, I've somehow managed to find time to
hack on things like this, and also use feedback from both PALindrome and some careful
audio recordings and test programs to "improve" the audio and video emulation of <html:a href="https://bbc.xania.org">jsbeeb</html:a>.
They make it arguably more authentic... but do sound and look objectively
worse -- the nostalgia hit is worth it though! All configurable of course (play with the settings
on the settings page or the top right for quick settings).</html:p>

<html:div class="footnote">
<html:hr />
<html:ol>
<html:li id="fn:cheap">
<html:p>Well, I say no-name but the instruction leaflet says "OIKWAN" and "Dongguan Auqun Industrial Co Ltd", so I suppose it's not completely nameless. <html:a class="footnote-backref" href="#fnref:cheap" title="Jump back to footnote 1 in the text">↩</html:a></html:p>
</html:li>
</html:ol>
</html:div>

    </html:div>

summary: Hooking a BBC Master up as a serial terminal to browse the web again
title: Recreating a 2010 Experiment
